title: Side-Effecting Queries (CQS Violations)
pattern: A method queries information from an object (returns a value) but also mutates the underlying state of the system as an observable side effect.
why_bad: Violates Bertrand Meyer's Command-Query Separation (CQS) principle: "Asking a question should not change the answer." It forces developers to read method implementation details to see if calling a simple getter will inadvertently mutate database values or logs, rendering testing and caching impossible.
detection: A method returning a non-void/non-Result type (e.g. `i64`, `String`) that also performs assignments to `self` fields or invokes other state-altering methods.
source: *Refactoring* by Martin Fowler (p. 279, "Separate Query from Modifier"); *Clean Code* by Robert C. Martin (Chapter 3, "Command Query Separation"); *Implementing Domain-Driven Design* by Vaughn Vernon (Chapter 10, "Side-Effect-Free Functions").
